title: Emrys and the Terminal
premise: Rafael Reyes, a xenolinguist whose dreams have drifted into alien syntax, pilots the courier ship Emrys along a dead trade route when she intercepts a distress call in Vessic — a language extinct for two hundred years, and the tongue of the enemy in humanity's long cold war. The signal leads her to a derelict station orbiting a dying star, where a reactor counts down toward detonation and a hidden archive holds proof that the war began on a lie manufactured by Rafael's own government. Torn between loyalty to the fleet that raised her and the truth that could free two species, she must decode and deliver the message before the countdown ends. In the end she broadcasts it to both fleets at once: the war collapses into uneasy truce, the station's last Vessic survivor dies holding her hand, and Rafael finally dreams again — this time in a language no one alive has ever spoken.
about_author: Vesper Almeida is a former radio astronomer who left observatory work to write about the silences between signals. They live aboard a converted ferry off the coast of Portugal, where they collect extinct alphabets and answer letters from readers in whatever language arrives first.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She runs the Emrys through the Meridian Gap, cataloguing worlds that have gone linguistically silent since the war froze all contact. Establishes her loneliness, her crew of two, and the ache of dreaming in languages she can't name. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Static Like a Voice
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A distress signal interrupts a supply stop at Thessaly Ring — structured, recursive, unmistakably Vessic. Her instruments insist the language died with the Vessic homeworld two centuries ago. Beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Crew of Two
chapters.summary: Engineer Sefa Okonkwo's POV. Sefa argues against answering the signal; protocol says report it to Fleet Command and move on. Rafael overrules her, and their friendship cracks along duty lines. Beat: loyalty tested before the journey truly begins.

chapters.title: Course Correction
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She files a falsified flight plan and burns for the signal's origin: Station Kestrel-9, orbiting a red dwarf at the war's old front line. First hints that someone in Fleet expected her to find this. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: What the Dream Said
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, dream sequence. She dreams in fluent Vessic for the first time — a voice counting down numbers she doesn't yet understand. Wakes with vocabulary she never learned. Beat: uncanny intimacy with an extinct tongue.

chapters.title: Kestrel-9
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The station appears intact but dark, its hull scarred by weapons fire from both sides. Docking clamps engage without permission. Something inside knows they've come. Beat: threshold crossing.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Inside, a reactor is already failing — forty days on the clock. The station's systems respond only to spoken Vessic, making Rafael the only key. Beat: stakes made physical and urgent.

chapters.title: Archive of Ashes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She finds the station's library: recordings, logs, a cultural archive preserved by someone who knew extinction was coming. Among them, a sealed message addressed 'to whoever still remembers.' Beat: grief and reverence.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Deep in hydroponics she finds Ilyen, an elderly Vessic archivist kept alive by failing machines — the last speaker of his language. He has been waiting two hundred years for a translator. Beat: meeting the heart of the story.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Their first conversation is halting, painful, beautiful; Ilyen corrects her grammar like a patient teacher. He reveals the archive contains proof the war's opening attack was staged. Beat: fragile trust established.

chapters.title: The Lie at the Beginning
chapters.summary: Ilyen's POV via translated log. Flashback structure: the Vessic recorded evidence that a human deep-cover operation destroyed their own colony to justify war. The message Ilyen guards is that proof. Beat: the moral fulcrum revealed.

chapters.title: Protocol
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa discovers what the message is and demands they destroy it or hand it to Fleet — releasing it could shatter the armistice and kill millions. Rafael refuses. Beat: open rupture between the crew.

chapters.title: Forty Days
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Montage chapter: translation sessions with Ilyen, reactor repairs, rationing, the countdown ticking in every scene. Rafael begins thinking in Vessic without noticing. Beat: deepening bonds under pressure.

chapters.title: Fleet Hails the Emrys
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Command contacts the ship: her false flight plan flagged, a patrol vessel dispatched to retrieve her. Captain Adeyemi, her old mentor, gives her one chance to come home quietly. Beat: authority closing in.

chapters.title: Mentor and Student
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. Comm-only chapter. Adeyemi reveals she knows about Kestrel-9 — Fleet has wanted the station erased for decades. She offers Rafael amnesty for silence. Beat: love expressed as coercion.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Loyalty
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael realizes her fluency isn't accident: Fleet trained her as a child on recovered Vessic material, grooming a translator for exactly this contingency. Her whole identity reframes as instrument. Beat: betrayal from within.

chapters.title: Ilyen's Warning
chapters.summary: Ilyen's POV. He tells Rafael the message cannot be given to one side alone — delivered partially, it becomes a weapon. It must reach both fleets simultaneously or not at all. Beat: the shape of the climax set.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Someone — or something automated — begins corrupting the archive. Sefa traces it to Fleet firmware buried in the Emrys's own systems. The ship itself is listening. Beat: paranoia takes hold.

chapters.title: Cutting Out the Ship's Tongue
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa physically strips the surveillance core while Rafael feeds it decoy translations. Their reconciliation begins here, forged in shared risk. Beat: repair of the broken friendship.

chapters.title: Day Twenty-Six
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Halfway. Ilyen's health fails; the machines keeping him alive draw power the reactor needs. He asks Rafael to let him die so the message survives. She refuses. Beat: love against duty, intimate scale.

chapters.title: The Patrol Arrives
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Adeyemi's vessel docks under pretense of rescue. Marines secure the station; Ilyen is taken into custody as an 'asset.' Rafael is confined to the Emrys. Beat: crushing defeat.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Language
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Fleet officers force Rafael to translate selectively, omitting the forgery evidence. She complies outwardly while seeding errors that will unravel later. Beat: resistance through craft.

chapters.title: What Sefa Carried
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Reveal: Sefa copied the full archive onto her personal implants weeks ago, betting on Rafael before Rafael bet on herself. Beat: loyalty answered with loyalty.

chapters.title: Ilyen Speaks to His Jailers
chapters.summary: Ilyen's POV. Under interrogation he speaks only Vessic, turning his extinction into armor — no one can question what no one understands except Rafael. Beat: dignity as defiance.

chapters.title: The Reactor Slips
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. With engineers diverted to security, containment falters; the countdown accelerates to nine days. Evacuation orders conflict with evidence-preservation orders. Beat: clock tightened.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Confession
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. Alone with Rafael, Adeyemi admits she helped bury the truth thirty years ago and has carried it like shrapnel ever since. She won't help — but she'll look away. Beat: complicity and mercy.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael, Sefa, and a sympathetic marine named Cortez plan the broadcast: hijack the station's deep-space array during the final evacuation window. Beat: the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Teaching the Dead Language to Machines
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Technical and tender: Rafael encodes the message for simultaneous transmission across both fleet networks, Ilyen dictating nuance from his sickbed. Beat: creation under sentence of death.

chapters.title: Cortez's Choice
chapters.summary: Cortez's POV. The young marine must decide between career and conscience; she disables the array's Fleet locks and walks away without looking back. Beat: ordinary courage.

chapters.title: Day Three
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Ilyen is dying faster than the reactor. He finishes the last annotation with Rafael's hand guiding his. He tells her the message was always meant to be finished by a stranger — that's why he waited. Beat: passing of the torch.

chapters.title: The Last Speaker
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Ilyen dies at dawn, station-time, mid-sentence, and Rafael completes the sentence aloud alone. She records herself speaking Vessic for the archive — becoming its second-to-last voice. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Evacuation Window
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Final day: crews abandon Kestrel-9, Adeyemi's ship withdraws on a technicality, and Sefa and Rafael stay behind against every order. Beat: deliberate isolation before the storm.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Climax part one: they seize the array and transmit the full message — history, forgery, Ilyen's testimony — to both fleets simultaneously as the reactor hits critical. Beat: the message leaves their hands forever.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Climax part two: the Emrys barely outruns the detonation; Kestrel-9 and Ilyen's body become light. Both fleets receive the transmission in the same second. Beat: catharsis through destruction.

chapters.title: Silence, Then Noise
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The aftermath hour: fleets hold fire, channels flood with argument, denial, and — slowly — verification requests. Rafael waits in the wreckage-light to learn if truth was enough. Beat: suspended breath.

chapters.title: The Armistice of Words
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. Fleet command fractures; Adeyemi testifies, choosing truth at last. A ceasefire is declared pending joint investigation. The war doesn't end — it stops. Beat: imperfect justice.

chapters.title: Inquiry
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael faces tribunal as hero and traitor simultaneously. She speaks her defense partly in Vessic, forcing the court to confront the language it tried to erase. Beat: accountability without erasure.

chapters.title: Sentence
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Verdict: stripped of rank, granted custody of the Vessic archive, assigned to found the first human–Vessic memory institute. Punishment shaped like a calling. Beat: bittersweet resolution.

chapters.title: Dreaming Again
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Months later, aboard the rebuilt Emrys teaching the archive to new students, Rafael dreams — and for the first time in years, the dream is in no language at all, just warmth. Beat: healing.

chapters.title: To Whoever Still Remembers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, coda. She records a new message for the archive, addressed to future listeners, echoing Ilyen's inscription. The route between worlds is reopening; somewhere, someone may answer. Beat: hope handed forward.
